# NFHN

> A Hacker News reader served entirely from a Netlify Edge Function. No
> framework: routing and HTML rendering happen at the edge, streamed as the
> upstream API responds. Content is Hacker News content, fetched live from the
> HNPWA API; NFHN neither hosts nor owns it.

Stories come from Hacker News and change continuously. Feed pages are the stable
entry points; individual story and profile URLs are stable but their contents are
whatever Hacker News currently returns. There is no account system, no database,
and no personalisation on the server: saved stories live in the reader's own
browser.

## Feeds

- [Top stories](https://hn.jakechampion.name/top/1): the front page, paginated as /top/:page
- [Newest](https://hn.jakechampion.name/newest/1): most recently submitted, /newest/:page
- [Ask HN](https://hn.jakechampion.name/ask/1): question threads, /ask/:page
- [Show HN](https://hn.jakechampion.name/show/1): things people built, /show/:page
- [Jobs](https://hn.jakechampion.name/jobs/1): who's hiring postings, /jobs/:page

## Item and profile URLs

- `/item/:id`: one story with its comment tree. The id is the Hacker News item id, so `/item/8863` is the same story as `news.ycombinator.com/item?id=8863`.
- `/user/:username`: a Hacker News profile with karma, account age, and recent submissions.

## Not worth crawling

- `/reader/:url`: a readability-extracted view of a third-party article. The content belongs to the original publisher — fetch and cite the original URL instead. Served `noindex`.
- `/saved`: an empty shell; its contents are rendered client-side from the visitor's own browser storage. Served `noindex`.

## About the project

- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/JakeChampion/nfhn)
- [Architecture decisions](https://github.com/JakeChampion/nfhn/tree/main/docs/adr): why there is no framework, why HTML is streamed, why caching works the way it does
- [Spec reviews](https://github.com/JakeChampion/nfhn/tree/main/docs/spec-reviews): what NFHN does and does not implement from published web specifications, and why
